argument: For K10 take R=Z_2[[Gamma]][G]=Z_2[[t]][G], where G is the fixed finite elementary abelian two-group, and take the free rank-two R-module T_2E tensor R with the actual continuous chi_0 psi kappa^(-1) action. R is a complete noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m generated by2,t and g-1 for g in G; its residue field is F_2. The actual finite quotients use J_(a,n)=(2^a,(1+t)^(2^n)-1). The quotient R/J_(a,n) is finite and local: modulo2 it is the group algebra of the finite two-group Gamma_n times G, whose augmentation ideal is nilpotent. Hence some power of m is contained in J_(a,n). Conversely J_(a,n) is contained in any prescribed m^k for a,n sufficiently large: 2^a is in m^k for a>=k, while for 1<=i<k the coefficient binomial(2^n,i) has valuation at least n-v_2(i), and terms of degree i>=k are already in m^k. Thus these ideals and the m-adic powers define cofinal filtrations. Use a diagonal cofinal sequence in a,n. Each H0 of the finite quotient coefficient is a subgroup of a finite module, so its images stabilize and lim1 H0 vanishes. Apply Corollary4.1.3 to the complete finite-type admissible R-module through this cofinal identification. Norm compatibility of the already supplied classes produces their inverse-limit element; the argument proves no new norm relation.
